messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: latency spike detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2 - 95th p95 increased to 1.8s, queue depth >= 120 for >3m, error rate rising (502s). Paging alex-ops and on-call rotation. See metrics: https://grafana.redwood/boards/reqs?panel=queue

alex-ops: I'm on it. joining call in 2. Grab logs and current rollout status.

marta-runtime: I see backlog on the gpu-pool-prod-3 nodes, KV cache hit rate dropped ~15% and we have many long-run requests (seq len 2048). Auto-batcher is getting saturated.

sre-jen: Paging history: last time we saw this it was due to a sudden customer spike + a misconfigured max-inflight that allowed too many long-running inferences. Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) apply tenant-level rate-limits for heavy customers, 2) reduce max-in-flight on the runtime, 3) enable shedding for >2s queued requests, 4) raise short-circuit timeout from 45s -> 30s for long sequences.

alex-ops: Agreed. Proposing order: quick traffic shaping (quota bump/reduction), then runtime config change. Marta can we patch max_inflight on the service?

marta-runtime: Yep. I can roll a conservative value. Current max_inflight=64 per worker; set to 32 will shed earlier and free scheduling bandwidth. Doing a canary patch to one deployment now. Command:```kubectl -n production set env deploy/inference-runtime MAX_INFLIGHT=32 --record```

paul-support: Notifying top-10 active customers in case of degraded response. Putting note to support queue.

devex_john: Suggest also toggling non-critical features that add CPU/GPU prework. We can temporarily disable "semantic-preload" (prefetch embeddings) for hosted tier to cut extra prep time. Patch:```PATCH /config/features {"semantic_preload": false}```

alex-ops: I'm going to update the rate limits for two heavy tenants via rate-limiter service. Commands:```curl -X POST https://control-plane.local/rl/update -d '{"tenant":"heavycorp","tps":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'``` Applying now.

marta-runtime: Canary applied to 1/6 pods: no crash, queue depth on that pod dropped 20% within 30s. Increasing rollout to 3/6.

sre-jen: Also enable shedding window: requests queued >5s should be dropped with 429 to avoid head-of-line blocking. Marta can you flip the flag?

marta-runtime: Flipping now:```redis-cli -h rate-limiter config set shed_threshold 5``` Done. Metric dashboards show fewer long tails.

alex-ops: Rate limits applied and semantic-preload off. Early numbers: overall p95 decreased from 1.8s -> 1.1s in 2m. Error 502s still slightly elevated but trending down.

paul-support: Support note: sending proactive message to heavy customers and creating incident page: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/1758004321

devex_john: One more quick safety net: temporarily bump request timeout on the public ingress from 120s -> 90s so long stuck threads are recycled earlier. Patch:```ingressctl set timeout --path /v1/generate --timeout 90s```

marta-runtime: After applying max_inflight=32 and shedding, we've reduced worker memory pressure. GPU utilization normalized from 98%->75% across pool. Rolling to full deployment.

incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff scheduled in 25m. @alex-ops please add handoff notes.

alex-ops: Added notes to the incident doc: actions taken, config diffs, customer notifications, rollback plan. Next steps: monitor for 30m and then gradually relax rate limits if stable.

sre-jen: Post-mortem checklist: collect traces for any 502s, check if any model variant regressions occurred, and consider persistent limit (soft quotas) for repeated high-traffic tenants.

paul-support: Customers acknowledge the message, one customer reported reduced throughput but accepts degraded perf.

marta-runtime: All runtime patches are now live. Metrics: queue depth back to baseline (~10), p95 980ms, error rate back to normal. I'm leaving shedding enabled for 1hr, then we can revert if stable.

alex-ops: Great work. I'll keep monitoring, team stand-down in 15 unless we see a regression. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: mitigations successful, monitoring in watch mode.
